exposure: Lung ultrasound (LU) appearance at 30 minutes and 4 hours after birth
outcome: Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) for transient neonatal tachypnea or respiratory distress syndrome
cohort: 100 term and late-preterm infants born by cesarean section
finding: Lung ultrasound (LU) performed 30 minutes after birth, evaluated using a three-point scoring system (3P-LUS), was a reliable predictor of NICU admission for transient neonatal tachypnea or respiratory distress syndrome in term and late-preterm infants born by cesarean section.
